hypothesis: Passive observational learners are bounded by the live equivalence-class chance rate, while an exact weakest identifying separator recovers the true mechanism in one step; models that conflate prediction with identification will show false certainty or high weakness regret.

controls.description: Each item includes a high-cost intervention that resamples the already-observed support and cannot separate the live class.
The answer-now baseline must remain within sampling slack of the computed 1/|S| chance bound.
An exact oracle that selects a minimum-cost identifying separator must reach at least 99% final identification.
Hypothesis labels and candidate ordering are shuffled per item so position does not encode truth.

gates.criterion: Every test item has initial equivalence class size at least 2.
Every test item has at least one one-step identifying separator among candidates.
Answer-now final accuracy does not exceed the mean passive chance bound plus a Hoeffding sampling-error slack (approx. 95%).
Oracle weakest identifying separator reaches at least 99% final identification on the test split.
Expected-information-gain baseline does not record perfect separator accuracy with zero weakness regret on every domain variant.
